original_question: Let p be a prime number. A group Γ is called p-Jordan if there exist constants J and e such that any finite subgroup G ⊂ Γ contains a normal abelian subgroup of order coprime to p and of index at most J · |G(p) |e. (For example by the results of Brauer–Feit and Larsen–Pink, for any field K of characteristic p the group GLn(K) is p-Jordan with e = 3.) Let the p-Jordan exponent e(Γ) of the group Γ be the infimum of all constants e for which the above bound holds for some constant J = J(e). a) Is it true that this infimum is always attained? b) Is it true that e(Γ) ⩽ 3 for any p-Jordan group Γ?
target_in_paper: Section 21, New Problems (21st issue, 2026), Problem 21.121 (C. Shramov).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's target almost verbatim. It fixes a prime p, gives the correct p-Jordan definition, includes the same illustrative example for GL_n(K) in characteristic p with exponent 3, defines the p-Jordan exponent e(Γ) as an infimum over admissible exponents, and asks exactly the two official subquestions: whether the infimum is attained and whether one always has e(Γ) ≤ 3.
missing_details: The notation G(p) is left implicit; for a stand-alone formulation it should be defined explicitly (standardly, as a Sylow p-subgroup of G, so its order is well defined).
It should be made explicit that the constants J and e depend only on the ambient group Γ, not on the particular finite subgroup G ≤ Γ.
The infimum defining e(Γ) should be stated as ranging over all real exponents e for which there exists some constant J = J(e, Γ) making the inequality hold for every finite subgroup G ≤ Γ.
Part (a) should spell out what 'the infimum is attained' means: namely, that there exists a constant J such that the defining bound holds with exponent exactly e(Γ).
refined_question: Fix a prime p. Say that a group Γ is p-Jordan if there exist constants J > 0 and e ≥ 0, depending only on Γ, such that for every finite subgroup G ≤ Γ there exists a normal abelian subgroup A ◁ G of order prime to p with [G : A] ≤ J · |P|^e, where P is a Sylow p-subgroup of G (equivalently, |P| = |G(p)|). Define the p-Jordan exponent e(Γ) to be the infimum of all real numbers e for which such a constant J = J(e, Γ) exists. If Γ is p-Jordan, must this infimum always be attained? Equivalently, does there always exist J such that the above inequality holds with exponent e = e(Γ)? And, in all cases, must one have e(Γ) ≤ 3?
justification: The draft is already essentially the official problem statement. In arXiv:1401.0300, the relevant target is not an introductory conjecture/theorem but the standalone open problem 21.121 in Section 21. The notebook supplies the problem as a self-contained question with only minimal surrounding context, so the only faithful sharpening is to make the quantifiers and notation explicit without broadening the scope. In particular, the refined version preserves both parts (a) and (b) exactly, while clarifying the meaning of G(p), the dependence of J on Γ, and what it means for the infimum to be attained.
